Each pair covers the **same eight seconds**: A is recorded, and B is synthesized from the four measured motor speeds. The generator was fitted to **32 other seconds of the same recording**; these are within-recording tests, not transfer to a new rig. FLY013 ran on the ground without propellers. FLY018 and FLY022 were airborne.

## Listen and look {#recordings}

Select a recording, press **Play**, then switch between **A · Recorded** and **B · Generated** without losing your place. Both use the same playback gain. Listen for the spacing and movement of the tones, the broadband hiss, and the balance between them—not a sample-by-sample waveform match. The spectrograms share a colour scale.

The matched comparison is at **16 kHz**. A separate **48 kHz original** lets you hear what lies outside the generator's band. No generated draw was selected by ear, and the metrics use unscaled waveforms.

## How the numbers and pictures are made {#numbers}

All quantities use the unscaled held-out WAV files at the model output rate. Let $r_c[n]$ be the recorded and $g_c[n]$ the generated sample of channel $c \in \{1,2\}$; full scale is 1.0.

**RMS level.** $L_c = 10\log_{10}\big(\tfrac1N\sum_n x_c[n]^2\big)$ dB for $x \in \{r, g\}$. 0 dB is RMS 1.0. This is a digital level, not a sound-pressure level.

**Welch PSD.** $P_c(f)$ is the one-sided power spectral density: Hann window of 0.512 s (8192 samples at 16 kHz), 50 % overlap, mean removed per segment, segments averaged.

**One-third-octave bands.** Band $b$ has the centre $f_b = 1000 \cdot 10^{k/10}$ Hz, $k = -13, -12, \dots$, and edges $f_b \cdot 10^{\pm 1/20}$. The first band is centred at 50 Hz. We keep every band whose upper edge is at most $0.49\,f_s$; at 16 kHz that is the 6.3 kHz band, so the scored range is 44.7 Hz – 7.08 kHz. Band power is $P_{c,b} = \sum_{f_k \in b} P_c(f_k)\,\Delta f$.

**Band difference.** $D_{c,b} = 10\log_{10}\big(P^{g}_{c,b} / P^{r}_{c,b}\big)$ dB. Positive means the model is louder in that band.

**Level error** (per channel) $= 10\log_{10}\big(\sum_b P^{g}_{c,b} / \sum_b P^{r}_{c,b}\big)$ dB: the broadband level difference over the scored band range.

**Band distance** $= \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2B}\sum_{c,b} D_{c,b}^2}$ dB over both channels and all $B$ bands. It splits exactly into a **band offset** $\bar D = \tfrac{1}{2B}\sum_{c,b} D_{c,b}$ and a **shape distance** $\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2B}\sum_{c,b} (D_{c,b} - \bar D)^2}$: band distance² = offset² + shape distance². The offset says "too loud or too quiet overall"; the shape distance says "wrong spectral balance". Lower is better for both distances. These are descriptive numbers for two examples, not a statistical test.

**Spectrograms.** Hann frames of 0.128 s (2048 samples at 16 kHz), hop 1/8 frame, power-spectrum scaling, averaged over the two channels, in dB re full scale². Both examples and both sources for a recording share a 70 dB colour range, with the upper limit 3 dB above the largest panel-wise 99.5th percentile (rounded up). The native-rate panel uses the same frame duration and colour scale. The lower strip shows short-time level.

## Model and fit

The generator is the repository's v4 regime noise model (`experiments.noise_model.flight_v4`), rendered to audio by `data_processing.noise_model.render`. It is fitted afresh to each recording. The renderer draws random phases from the fitted model and uses the measured rotor speeds of the held-out window; it applies no level normalisation. Each recording's tab lists the optimizer, objective, configuration and convergence exactly as the fit reported them, together with the fit's own limitations.

The model output and the matched recording share one sample rate. The scored band range stops below that rate's Nyquist frequency. Content above it — for example high motor orders of FLY013 — appears only in the native-rate player and figure.

## Provenance

The page embeds only audio excerpts, figures and summary numbers. It contains no rotor-speed traces or other raw sensor data. Host paths in the fit metadata are reduced to file names.
